about.text: Époisses, also known as Époisses de Bourgogne, is a legally demarcated cheese made in the village of Époisses and its environs, in the département of Côte-d'Or, about halfway between Dijon and Auxerre, in the former duchy of Burgundy, France, from agricultural processes and resources traditionally found in that region.

how.label: wash in marc
how.text: A slow, mostly lactic set gives a fragile, moist curd that is ladled with little cutting and left to drain by itself. Repeated washing with marc de Bourgogne water during at least four weeks develops the brick-red colour and pungent aroma of the rind.

steps.note: Mostly by lactic coagulation, with rennet the only coagulant allowed.
Roughly, without breaking up the curd.
Into cylinders of 95–115 mm (250–350 g) or 165–190 mm (700–1100 g).
Washed with water containing marc de Bourgogne.
